personality_one_liner: A high-contrast, rugged command center built for emergency scanning, rapid action, and live tracking on the road.

spacing.rule: Dense but scannable hierarchy. Generous padding around the primary emergency CTA, tighter spacing in data-heavy service dashboards.

do's: Use solid dark surfaces (surfaceSecondary) for bottom sheets and cards to maintain high readability.
dont's: Avoid glassmorphism on map bottom sheets or emergency CTAs; clarity and contrast beat aesthetics here.

screens.name: Home (Map & Request)
screens.purpose: A map-first experience allowing stranded users to request help in maximum 2 taps.

states.loading: Full-screen dark asphalt texture with a pulsing yellow loader.
states.empty: Map view with a bottom sheet showing 'Select Issue'.
states.error: Bottom sheet displays red error banner: 'Unable to locate mechanics. Retry?'

screens.layout: Full-screen map map view using a dark map style. A persistent @gorhom/bottom-sheet at the bottom. The sheet contains horizontally scrollable issue chips (Puncture, Engine, Battery, Fuel). Below the chips is a massive, full-width brandPrimary CTA reading 'REQUEST HELP NOW' (min 56pt height). An SOS FAB floats above the bottom sheet on the right side.

screens.name: Live Tracking
screens.purpose: Shows the mechanic's ETA and location on the map, providing a sense of safety.

states.loading: Skeleton of mechanic details and route.
states.empty: N/A - screen only accessed when tracking.
states.error: Offline Mode banner: 'Network low. Tracking via SMS updates.'

screens.layout: Map with a route polyline. Bottom sheet expanded to show Mechanic profile (real photo), ETA in large Barlow Condensed text, vehicle details, and two large buttons: 'Call' and 'Message'.

screens.name: Provider Dashboard
screens.purpose: Command center for mechanics to accept/reject incoming emergency requests and view earnings.

states.loading: Spinning loader over the stats grid.
states.empty: Illustration of a mechanic tools with 'No active requests right now. You are online.'

screens.layout: Top header with an 'Online/Offline' toggle. A 2-column grid showing 'Today's Earnings' and 'Requests'. Below that, a list of incoming or active requests on surfaceSecondary cards with clear 'Accept' (brandPrimary) and 'Decline' (surfaceTertiary) buttons.

screens.name: AI Issue Detection
screens.purpose: Allows users to take a photo of their breakdown for AI-based issue categorization.

states.loading: Analyzing photo with a scanning line animation over the image.
states.empty: Camera viewfinder with 'Take a photo of the problem'.
states.error: Error modal: 'Could not identify issue. Please select manually.'

screens.layout: Camera view or photo preview covering the top 60% of the screen. Bottom 40% surfaceSecondary container with detected issue results as selectable chips and a 'Confirm & Request' sticky CTA.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility DARK personality. This is a rugged, emergency-focused app, not a luxury or playful one. Avoid rounded, soft, or playful components.
Implement the map as the full-screen root component on the Home screen. All interactions (issue selection, requesting help) must happen via the `@gorhom/bottom-sheet`.
The primary CTA ('REQUEST HELP NOW') must be massive (min 56pt height), use `brandPrimary` (#FFD600), and feature bold `Barlow Condensed` typography.
Ensure contrast is ultra-high. Use `surfaceSecondary` (#1C1F22) for cards and sheets to stand out from the `surface` (#111315) background without relying on glassmorphism or shadows.
For the Service Provider Dashboard, emphasize glanceability with oversized metrics and segmented controls. The design should look like a command center.
Use Phosphor icons in filled/bold weights to maintain the rugged aesthetic.
Banned hues: NO blue, purple, indigo, or orange. Stick strictly to the asphalt, safety yellow, and red palette defined.
All cards containing images must use the gradient-to-dark scrim pattern to guarantee text readability.
